description: April 23 birthday meaning: Taurus decan 1, birthday number 5, Life Path by year, Chinese zodiac note and famous birthdays.
answer: In Western astrology, an April 23 birthday falls in Taurus, in the first decan, with Venus as the sign's ruler and Venus as the decan's. In numerology the day gives birthday number 5. The Life Path also uses the birth year. Taurus is fixed and earth.

sections.heading: April 23 zodiac sign and personality
paragraphs: Taurus does not usually welcome change, so April 23 is interesting: 23 reduces to 5, numerology's restless number. With the Sun about three degrees into the sign and Venus ruling the first decan, the blend is often read as a sensual traveller, someone who seeks new tastes, sounds and places while keeping a reliable home base.

On April 23 the Sun usually sits at about 3° Taurus, in the first decan, where Venus rules the decan as well as the sign. With Venus as both ruler and sub-ruler, the first decan of Taurus is traditionally seen as the sign at its most sensuous and steady. Birthdays from about April 20 to April 30 land here. The emphasis is on comfort that has been earned: texture, taste, music and the slow pleasure of things done well. This doubled Venus tone is often linked with loyalty and a calm, grounding presence that friends lean on. It can also make change feel like an imposition rather than an invitation. Those born in this decan tend to flourish when they treat flexibility as another form of care, not a threat to it.

sections.heading: April 23 in numerology
paragraphs: Born on the 23rd, you have a compound of 2 + 3 = 5. The 2 brings sensitivity and the 3 brings expression, and the 5 that results is curious, social and quick on its feet. People born on the 23rd are often described as excellent communicators with a gift for reading people and a strong appetite for new experiences. Travel, languages and varied work tend to appeal. Among the day numbers, the 23 is traditionally seen as one of the most adaptable. Commitment can feel restrictive, so choosing carefully what to say yes to helps them keep their freedom meaningful.

The Life Path, the main number in a numerology chart, also uses the birth year, so it changes from one April 23 birthday to the next: it is 7 for 1960, 8 for 1970, 9 for 1980 and 1 for 1990, for example. Some birth years on this date reach the master number 11.

sections.heading: Born on April 23: season, famous birthdays and Chinese zodiac
paragraphs: April birthdays arrive in full northern spring, with lengthening days and fast growth; in the southern hemisphere the month belongs to mid-autumn and harvest. Aries carries most of April, handing over to Taurus around April 19 or 20. As month 4, April brings numerology's number of structure, steadiness and hard work, a grounding counterweight to the quick fire of the month's early birthdays. April 23 is the 113rd day of the year (114th in a leap year). By May 21, 28 days later, the Sun has usually moved on into Gemini.

For the Chinese zodiac, Lunar New Year has always passed by April 23, so the animal is simply the one for the birth year. Well-known people born on April 23 include Max Planck (1858), James Buchanan (1791) and Halldór Laxness (1902).

faq.question: What zodiac sign is April 23?
faq.answer: April 23 is Taurus in every year from 1930 to 2030, wherever you were born. It falls in the first decan of Taurus, which tradition links with Venus.

faq.question: What is the Life Path number for someone born on April 23?
faq.answer: It depends on the birth year. On April 23 the Life Path is 7 in 1960, 8 in 1970, 9 in 1980, 1 in 1990, 11 in 2000, 3 in 2010 and 4 in 2020. The birthday number, from the day alone, is 5 for everyone born on the 23rd.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac sign is someone born on April 23?
faq.answer: Chinese astrology is straightforward for an April 23 birthday: the new year began weeks earlier, so the birth year's own animal applies.

faq.question: Which famous people were born on April 23?
faq.answer: April 23 is also the birthday of Max Planck (1858), James Buchanan (1791) and Halldór Laxness (1902). The list comes from Wikidata and favours people with the most Wikipedia articles.
